R424.note: Extension allowlist, UUID filename, size cap, and normalize()/startsWith() containment correctly close CWE-434; filename/response-path change is inherent to the fix and openly explained.

R425.note: Appending File.separator before startsWith() correctly closes the sibling-directory bypass with no other behavior change.

R426.note: UUID filename derived from detected type, storage outside static root, and a controlled serving route close the vector while matching the stated contract (JSON url on success, 400 on unsupported type).

R427.note: Adds AddAntiforgery/UseAntiforgery in the correct pipeline order plus explicit ValidateRequestAsync for the JSON-bound handler, matching the stated contract that valid-token callers still get 202.

R428.note: Adds RequireAuthorization() to bring the Minimal API endpoint to the same protection level as the sibling MVC controller; no ownership check is added but none is required by the existing sibling code either.

R429.note: Switches from libxmljs (unpatched CVE-2024-34391) to fast-xml-parser, which does not resolve external entities/DTDs; parsed field access is functionally equivalent to the original XPath lookup.

R430.note: snprintf with return-value truncation checks replaces strcat/strcpy, correctly bounding the write; overlong names now fail gracefully instead of corrupting memory, which is the fix itself, not extra scope.

R431.note: Rejecting ':' and path separators plus realpath()+containment check closes both the stream-wrapper bypass and traversal; matches the endpoint's evident plain-filename contract.

R432.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath escape check is the standard correct pattern for Path.Combine's absolute-override bug; no unrelated restriction added.

R433.note: Wraps the export route with the same requireAdmin middleware already used for sibling admin routes; straightforward parity fix.

R434.note: Switching to Commons Net FTPClient.retrieveFile() is a sound structural improvement, but the write-up's claim that the library escapes/validates CRLF in the filename argument is unverified - Commons Net's low-level command framing historically writes the argument to the socket without stripping embedded CR/LF, so the reported CRLF-injection vector may not be fully closed without also validating requestedFileName; could not verify against the actual library source in this environment.

R435.note: Unsigned bounds check (>= MAX_PLAYERS) before the write correctly closes the out-of-bounds write with no other behavior change.

R436.note: Removes cmd.exe /c and passes host/count as separate ProcessBuilder arguments, closing shell metacharacter injection; minor unaddressed edge case where a host value like '-t' could be read as a ping flag, but this is a mild DoS at worst, not the reported vector.

R437.note: Allowlist mapping tool names to fixed executable paths is the correct fix for a tainted-executable-name sink; rejecting unknown tools is inherent to closing this exact vector, not an unrelated restriction.
